title: Customer Complaint Handling Process
text:
Document: Customer Complaint Handling Process
Section: Complaint Channels

Customers may raise complaints through the dealer directly, the manufacturer's customer care line, or the online feedback portal. All channels feed into the centralized Customer Relations Management (CRM) system.

title: Customer Complaint Handling Process
text:
Document: Customer Complaint Handling Process
Section: Response Time Standards

| Severity | Initial Response | Resolution Target |
|---|---|---|
| Critical (safety-related) | Within 4 hours | Within 48 hours |
| High (vehicle non-operational) | Within 24 hours | Within 5 business days |
| Standard (service/billing dispute) | Within 48 hours | Within 10 business days |

title: Customer Complaint Handling Process
text:
Document: Customer Complaint Handling Process
Section: Escalation Path

If a dealer cannot resolve a complaint within the target window, it is automatically escalated to the Regional Customer Relations team. Unresolved escalations beyond 15 business days are reviewed by the National Customer Experience team.

title: Customer Complaint Handling Process
text:
Document: Customer Complaint Handling Process
Section: Goodwill Adjustments

Dealers may offer goodwill gestures (service discounts, loaner extensions) up to $300 in value without approval. Larger goodwill requests require regional manager sign-off, submitted via the Goodwill Request form.

title: Customer Complaint Handling Process
text:
Document: Customer Complaint Handling Process
Section: Documentation

All complaint interactions must be logged in the CRM with timestamps, including phone calls and in-person conversations, to maintain an auditable resolution history.

title: New Dealer Onboarding Process
text:
Document: New Dealer Onboarding Process
Section: Step 1: Application & Approval

Prospective dealers submit an application through the Regional Partner Portal, including business license, facility photos, and projected sales volume. Approval typically takes 3–4 weeks.

title: New Dealer Onboarding Process
text:
Document: New Dealer Onboarding Process
Section: Step 2: Systems Access

Once approved, dealers receive credentials for:
- Dealer Management System (DMS) — inventory, sales, and customer records
- Parts Ordering Portal — for ordering parts and accessories
- Service Portal — for scheduling and warranty claims

title: New Dealer Onboarding Process
text:
Document: New Dealer Onboarding Process
Section: Step 3: Training Requirements

All dealer staff must complete the mandatory 2-day onboarding training covering:
- Sales and financing procedures
- Warranty claim submission
- Customer service standards

Sales staff must additionally complete product certification training for each vehicle line they sell, renewed annually.

title: New Dealer Onboarding Process
text:
Document: New Dealer Onboarding Process
Section: Step 4: Initial Inventory Allocation

New dealers receive an initial inventory allocation based on projected volume, typically 15–25 vehicles across core model lines. Allocation is reviewed quarterly based on sales performance.

title: New Dealer Onboarding Process
text:
Document: New Dealer Onboarding Process
Section: Ongoing Compliance

Dealers are audited annually for facility standards, customer satisfaction scores, and compliance with brand presentation guidelines. Dealers falling below a 3.5/5.0 customer satisfaction average for two consecutive quarters enter a formal improvement plan.

title: Dealer Portal Access & Permissions
text:
Document: Dealer Portal Access & Permissions
Section: User Roles

| Role | Access Level |
|---|---|
| Sales Associate | Inventory viewing, customer records (read-only for pricing) |
| Service Advisor | Service scheduling, warranty claims, parts ordering |
| Dealer Principal | Full access, including financial reports and staff management |
| Regional Admin | Cross-dealer visibility within assigned region |

title: Dealer Portal Access & Permissions
text:
Document: Dealer Portal Access & Permissions
Section: Password & Security Policy

Portal passwords must be reset every 90 days and meet minimum complexity requirements (12+ characters, mixed case, numbers, symbols). Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all Dealer Principal and Regional Admin accounts.

title: Dealer Portal Access & Permissions
text:
Document: Dealer Portal Access & Permissions
Section: Account Lockout

Accounts are locked after 5 consecutive failed login attempts. Unlock requests must go through the IT Service Desk with identity verification.

title: Dealer Portal Access & Permissions
text:
Document: Dealer Portal Access & Permissions
Section: Access Revocation

When staff leave a dealership, access must be revoked within 24 hours by the Dealer Principal or Regional Admin. Failure to revoke access in a timely manner may affect the dealership's compliance audit score.

title: Dealer Portal Access & Permissions
text:
Document: Dealer Portal Access & Permissions
Section: Support Contact

Technical issues with the portal should be logged through the IT Service Desk ticketing system, with a standard response SLA of 4 business hours.

title: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
text:
Document: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
Section: Overview

Dealers may offer customers optional extended warranty plans beyond the standard coverage period.

title: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
text:
Document: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
Section: Available Plans

| Plan Name | Duration | Mileage Limit | Price (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Essential Plus | +2 years | +40,000 miles | $899 |
| Comprehensive | +4 years | +80,000 miles | $1,599 |
| Premium Care | +6 years | +120,000 miles | $2,299 |

title: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
text:
Document: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
Section: Eligibility

Extended warranties must be purchased within 90 days of the original vehicle sale date. Vehicles older than 1 year or with more than 15,000 miles at time of purchase are not eligible.

title: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
text:
Document: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
Section: What's Covered

All Premium Care and Comprehensive plans cover the same components as the Standard Warranty, plus:
- Navigation and infotainment electronics
- Hybrid/EV battery systems (Premium Care only)
- Roadside assistance for the duration of the plan

title: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
text:
Document: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
Section: Cancellation

Customers may cancel an extended warranty within 30 days of purchase for a full refund, provided no claims have been filed. After 30 days, refunds are prorated based on remaining coverage.

title: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
text:
Document: Extended Warranty Purchase Options
Section: Dealer Commission

Dealers receive a 12% commission on each extended warranty plan sold, paid out in the following month's settlement cycle.

title: Customer Financing & Incentive Programs
text:
Document: Customer Financing & Incentive Programs
Section: Standard Financing

Customers may finance through the manufacturer's preferred lending partner at rates starting from 3.9% APR for qualified buyers (credit score 700+), with terms from 24 to 72 months.

title: Customer Financing & Incentive Programs
text:
Document: Customer Financing & Incentive Programs
Section: Current Incentive Programs

| Program | Details | Expiry |
|---|---|---|
| First-Time Buyer Credit | $1,000 off MSRP | Ongoing |
| Military & Veteran Discount | $750 off MSRP | Ongoing |
| Loyalty Trade-In Bonus | $500 additional trade-in value for existing owners | Reviewed quarterly |
| Seasonal Clearance | Up to $2,000 off select 2024 model-year inventory | Ends when inventory depleted |

title: Customer Financing & Incentive Programs
text:
Document: Customer Financing & Incentive Programs
Section: Lease Options

Lease terms are available on select models (Sedan EX, SUV Touring) with terms of 24 or 36 months. Standard mileage allowance is 12,000 miles/year, with a $0.20/mile excess fee.

title: Customer Financing & Incentive Programs
text:
Document: Customer Financing & Incentive Programs
Section: Dealer-Administered Discounts

Dealers may apply discretionary discounts up to 5% of MSRP without regional approval. Discounts exceeding 5% require regional sales manager sign-off, logged in the DMS.

title: Customer Financing & Incentive Programs
text:
Document: Customer Financing & Incentive Programs
Section: Documentation Required for Financing

Proof of income, valid ID, and proof of residence are required for all financing applications. Pre-approval decisions are typically returned within 15 minutes through the lending partner's portal.

title: Inventory Lookup FAQ
section: How do I check current stock for a part?
text:
Document: Inventory Lookup FAQ
Section: How do I check current stock for a part?

General stocking patterns and reorder thresholds are described below. For the exact current quantity of a specific part at a specific warehouse, dealers must query the live Inventory system, since stock levels change continuously throughout the day and are not captured in static reference material.

title: Inventory Lookup FAQ
text:
Document: Inventory Lookup FAQ
Section: Standard Reorder Thresholds

Parts are automatically reordered when stock falls below the following thresholds:
- High-velocity parts (filters, fluids): reorder at 20% of max stock
- Medium-velocity parts (brakes, batteries): reorder at 30% of max stock
- Low-velocity parts (special-order electrical): manual reorder only

title: Inventory Lookup FAQ
text:
Document: Inventory Lookup FAQ
Section: Warehouse Network

The distribution network consists of 4 regional warehouses. Standard shipping time from warehouse to dealer is 1–3 business days depending on region.

title: Inventory Lookup FAQ
text:
Document: Inventory Lookup FAQ
Section: Backorder Handling

If a part is out of stock across all warehouses, it is marked as backordered and dealers receive an estimated restock date, typically updated weekly until the part is available again.

title: Dealer Inventory Management Guidelines
text:
Document: Dealer Inventory Management Guidelines
Section: Inventory Allocation

Vehicle inventory is allocated monthly based on a dealer's trailing 90-day sales velocity, regional demand forecasts, and facility capacity. Allocation requests can be adjusted via the Inventory Planning tool.

title: Dealer Inventory Management Guidelines
text:
Document: Dealer Inventory Management Guidelines
Section: Minimum Stocking Requirements

Dealers are required to maintain a minimum of 10 units per core model line to remain in good standing for allocation priority. Falling below this threshold for 60 consecutive days triggers a review.

title: Dealer Inventory Management Guidelines
text:
Document: Dealer Inventory Management Guidelines
Section: Inter-Dealer Transfers

Dealers may request a transfer of a specific vehicle from another dealer's lot through the Inter-Dealer Trade system. Transfers require mutual agreement and typically incur a $150 logistics fee, split evenly unless otherwise negotiated.

title: Dealer Inventory Management Guidelines
text:
Document: Dealer Inventory Management Guidelines
Section: Aged Inventory

Vehicles on a dealer's lot for more than 120 days are flagged as "aged inventory" and become eligible for manufacturer-supported clearance pricing, reducing dealer floorplan interest costs.

title: Dealer Inventory Management Guidelines
text:
Document: Dealer Inventory Management Guidelines
Section: Floorplan Financing

Dealers finance inventory through floorplan credit lines, with interest accruing daily until the vehicle is sold. Interest rates are reviewed quarterly based on the prime rate plus an agreed margin.

title: Order Status & Tracking FAQ
text:
Document: Order Status & Tracking FAQ
Section: How is order status determined?

Orders move through four stages: Placed → Processing → Shipped → Delivered. Status updates are generated automatically from the logistics system and typically refresh every 4 hours.

title: Order Status & Tracking FAQ
text:
Document: Order Status & Tracking FAQ
Section: Note on Real-Time Lookups

This document provides general guidance only. For the current status of a specific order, dealers should query the live Order Status system directly using the order ID, as statuses change frequently and are not reflected in static documentation.

title: Order Status & Tracking FAQ
text:
Document: Order Status & Tracking FAQ
Section: Typical Processing Times

| Order Type | Typical Processing Time |
|---|---|
| In-stock parts | 1–2 business days |
| Special-order parts | 10–15 business days |
| Vehicle factory orders | 6–10 weeks |

title: Order Status & Tracking FAQ
text:
Document: Order Status & Tracking FAQ
Section: Delayed Orders

Orders exceeding their expected timeframe by more than 5 business days are automatically flagged for review by the logistics team, and dealers receive a proactive notification with a revised estimate.

title: Order Status & Tracking FAQ
text:
Document: Order Status & Tracking FAQ
Section: Order Cancellation

Orders may be cancelled free of charge before they reach "Processing" status. Once an order enters "Processing," a cancellation fee of 10% of order value may apply for special-order items.

title: Vehicle Recall Procedures
text:
Document: Vehicle Recall Procedures
Section: Recall Notification

When a recall is issued, affected dealers are notified via the Service Portal within 24 hours, with a list of affected VINs in their sales/service territory. Customers are notified by mail per regulatory requirements within 5 business days.

title: Vehicle Recall Procedures
text:
Document: Vehicle Recall Procedures
Section: Dealer Responsibilities

1. Check incoming service vehicles against the active recall list before any other work is performed.
2. Perform recall remedies at no cost to the customer, regardless of warranty status.
3. Submit recall completion records through the Warranty Claims system within 48 hours of completion.

title: Vehicle Recall Procedures
text:
Document: Vehicle Recall Procedures
Section: Parts Availability for Recalls

Recall-related parts are prioritized in the supply chain and typically ship within 3–5 business days of a claim being logged, faster than standard parts orders.

title: Vehicle Recall Procedures
text:
Document: Vehicle Recall Procedures
Section: Customer Communication

If a required part is on backorder, dealers must log a temporary measure (if applicable, e.g., a safety advisory) and provide the customer an estimated remedy date, updated weekly until resolved.

title: Vehicle Recall Procedures
text:
Document: Vehicle Recall Procedures
Section: Reporting

Dealers must report any safety-related complaint potentially linked to a known or suspected defect within 24 hours via the Safety Issues hotline, separate from standard warranty claims.

title: Vehicle Return and Exchange Policy
text:
Document: Vehicle Return and Exchange Policy
Section: New Vehicle Returns

New vehicles may be returned within 5 calendar days of delivery, provided the vehicle has fewer than 250 miles on the odometer and shows no signs of damage or modification. A restocking fee of $500 applies to all approved returns.

title: Vehicle Return and Exchange Policy
text:
Document: Vehicle Return and Exchange Policy
Section: Parts Returns

Unused, unopened parts may be returned within 45 days of purchase with original receipt and packaging for a full refund. Electrical components and special-order parts are non-returnable once the packaging has been opened.

title: Vehicle Return and Exchange Policy
text:
Document: Vehicle Return and Exchange Policy
Section: Exchange Process

1. Dealer submits a return request through the Dealer Portal under "Returns & Exchanges."
2. Regional manager approval is required for any return involving a vehicle with more than 100 miles.
3. Approved returns are processed within 7–10 business days, with funds credited to the dealer's account.

title: Vehicle Return and Exchange Policy
text:
Document: Vehicle Return and Exchange Policy
Section: Non-Returnable Items

- Custom or special-order parts
- Floor mats, seat covers, or installed accessories
- Any item marked "Final Sale" in the catalog

title: Vehicle Return and Exchange Policy
text:
Document: Vehicle Return and Exchange Policy
Section: Damaged or Defective Items

If a part arrives damaged or defective, dealers should file a claim within 48 hours of receipt via the Quality Issues form, including photos of the damage. Replacement parts are shipped at no additional cost once approved.

title: Service Appointment Scheduling Policy
text:
Document: Service Appointment Scheduling Policy
Section: Booking Windows

Service appointments can be booked up to 60 days in advance through the Dealer Service Portal or by phone. Same-day appointments are subject to bay availability and are not guaranteed.

title: Service Appointment Scheduling Policy
text:
Document: Service Appointment Scheduling Policy
Section: Standard Service Slot Durations

| Service Type | Standard Duration |
|---|---|
| Oil change & inspection | 45 minutes |
| Brake pad replacement | 90 minutes |
| Tire rotation | 30 minutes |
| Full diagnostic scan | 60 minutes |
| Major service (60k/100k mile) | 3–4 hours |

title: Service Appointment Scheduling Policy
text:
Document: Service Appointment Scheduling Policy
Section: Cancellation & Rescheduling

Customers may cancel or reschedule up to 2 hours before the appointment without penalty. Same-day cancellations after the 2-hour window may incur a $25 no-show fee, at dealer discretion.

title: Service Appointment Scheduling Policy
text:
Document: Service Appointment Scheduling Policy
Section: Loaner Vehicle Policy

Loaner vehicles are available for services expected to exceed 4 hours, subject to availability. Customers must present a valid driver's license and proof of insurance.

title: Service Appointment Scheduling Policy
text:
Document: Service Appointment Scheduling Policy
Section: Priority Scheduling

Customers with an active extended warranty plan (see Extended Warranty Options) receive priority scheduling, with guaranteed appointment slots within 48 hours of request.

title: Vehicle Trade-In Valuation Policy
text:
Document: Vehicle Trade-In Valuation Policy
Section: Valuation Process

Trade-in vehicles are appraised using the internal valuation tool, which factors in mileage, condition, market demand, and accident history (via vehicle history report). Appraisals are valid for 7 days.

title: Vehicle Trade-In Valuation Policy
text:
Document: Vehicle Trade-In Valuation Policy
Section: Condition Categories

| Category | Description | Typical Value Adjustment |
|---|---|---|
| Excellent | No visible wear, full service history | Base valuation |
| Good | Minor cosmetic wear, routine maintenance | -5% to -8% |
| Fair | Noticeable wear, some deferred maintenance | -12% to -18% |
| Poor | Mechanical issues or significant damage | -25% or more, case-by-case |

title: Vehicle Trade-In Valuation Policy
text:
Document: Vehicle Trade-In Valuation Policy
Section: Outstanding Loan Balances

If the trade-in vehicle has an outstanding loan balance exceeding the appraised value (negative equity), the difference may be rolled into the new vehicle financing, subject to lender approval.

title: Vehicle Trade-In Valuation Policy
text:
Document: Vehicle Trade-In Valuation Policy
Section: Required Documentation

- Vehicle title or current registration
- Valid ID matching the title holder
- Loan payoff statement (if applicable)

title: Vehicle Trade-In Valuation Policy
text:
Document: Vehicle Trade-In Valuation Policy
Section: Dealer Discretion

Dealers may offer up to 10% above the system-generated appraisal as a competitive incentive, logged with justification in the DMS trade-in module.

title: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
text:
Document: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
Section: Overview

All new vehicles sold through authorized dealers are covered under the Standard Limited Warranty for 3 years or 60,000 miles, whichever occurs first. This warranty covers defects in materials and workmanship for all factory-installed components.

title: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
text:
Document: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
Section: Coverage Includes

- Engine and transmission components
- Electrical systems (factory-installed)
- Air conditioning and heating systems
- Factory-installed infotainment systems

title: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
text:
Document: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
Section: Coverage Excludes

- Tires (covered separately under manufacturer tire warranty)
- Wear items: brake pads, wiper blades, light bulbs
- Damage from accidents, misuse, or unauthorized modifications
- Routine maintenance items (oil changes, filter replacements)

title: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
text:
Document: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
Section: Powertrain Extended Warranty

The powertrain (engine, transmission, drivetrain) is covered for an additional period of 5 years or 100,000 miles under the Extended Powertrain Warranty, automatically included at no extra cost.

title: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
text:
Document: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
Section: Claim Process

Dealers must submit a warranty claim through the internal claims portal within 30 days of the repair date. Claims require: VIN, odometer reading, description of defect, and diagnostic report. Claims are typically reviewed within 5 business days.

title: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
text:
Document: Standard Vehicle Warranty Policy
Section: Transferability

The warranty is transferable to a second owner if the vehicle is sold privately within the original coverage period. No transfer fee applies.
